_meta.description: Stylistic archetypes per position with verified academy bios sourced from public biographical data (Wikipedia, Transfermarkt, FBref, club academy pages, long-form journalism). Each archetype includes signature_attrs (must-have score gates), anchor (weighted attrs for the style lens), profile (foot/build/role/path — used by the build, role and path lenses), and academy_bio (age-bracketed biographical facts used for age-aware comparisons). NEVER publishes numeric youth scores for any named professional — only sourced biographical facts.
_meta.last_filled: academy_bio full parity for GK + ST + W + CB + FB + DM + CM

attacking midfielder.name: Modric-type composer
attacking midfielder.summary: Composed playmaker who controls tempo with scanning and elite ball-handling.

academy_bio.8-10: Started in NK Zadar's youth section around age 6, growing up in Croatia during the war. Always the smallest in his age group but already known locally for not losing the ball.
academy_bio.11-12: Around U12 was tried at Hajduk Split (Croatia's biggest academy) — rejected for being 'too thin and small to make it'. Returned to NK Zadar and kept playing weekly.
academy_bio.13-14: U13-U14 at NK Zadar — small playmaker, dropped deep to receive because he wasn't tall enough to win duels higher up. Caught Dinamo Zagreb scouts' attention at youth tournaments.
academy_bio.15-17: Signed by Dinamo Zagreb academy at 16. Senior first-team debut at 17 — composure under pressure was already first-team quality before the legs caught up.
academy_bio.18-21: Loaned to Zrinjski Mostar (Bosnian league) at 18 to toughen up physically. Returned to Dinamo at 19 as a regular. Tottenham at 22, Real Madrid at 26.

attacking midfielder.career_brief: Career: 750+ club appearances · 180+ Croatia caps · 6× UEFA Champions League winner · Ballon d'Or 2018 · UEFA Player of the Year 2017-18 · 4 La Liga titles with Real Madrid · FBref career pass completion ~88% across 13 La Liga seasons.

attacking midfielder.name: Ödegaard-type composer
attacking midfielder.summary: Arsenal's brain — composes the side with elite scanning and weight.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined Strømsgodset (Drammen, Norway) youth around age 7. Father Hans Erik was a Norwegian pro, so football was the family rhythm from very young.
academy_bio.11-12: U12 at Strømsgodset — already known in Norwegian junior football for picking out a pass other kids couldn't see. Skipped most U13 youth football to train with older boys.
academy_bio.13-14: U13-U14 at Strømsgodset — training regularly with U16 and U18 squads. Norwegian FA flagged him as the most talented academy product in a generation.
academy_bio.15-17: Senior Strømsgodset debut at 15 — became the youngest player in Tippeligaen history. Sold to Real Madrid at 16 for ~€3m. Spent 16-21 on loan tours (Heerenveen, Vitesse, Real Sociedad, Arsenal).
academy_bio.18-21: Loan years at Heerenveen, Vitesse and Real Sociedad shaped the modern Ödegaard — added composure under physical pressure. Permanent Arsenal move at 22, captain by 23.

attacking midfielder.career_brief: Career: Real Sociedad loan was the turning point — 7 goals & 9 assists in his breakthrough La Liga season. Arsenal captain at 23. Premier League most assists 2022-23 (10). Norway captain since age 20. Norwegian Player of the Year 5× consecutively (2019-23).

attacking midfielder.name: Pedri-type press-breaker
attacking midfielder.summary: Press-resistant micro-genius — escapes pressure to find the next pass.

academy_bio.8-10: Started in Tegueste (small village in Tenerife, Canary Islands) around age 6 at the local club Juventud Laguna — playing barefoot in family yards before that.
academy_bio.11-12: Joined CD Tegueste U12 — already a head shorter than his teammates but rarely lost the ball in tight space.
academy_bio.13-14: Joined UD Las Palmas (Canary Islands pro club) academy at 14. Coaches said he was the only kid who 'played with his head up since the day he arrived'.
academy_bio.15-17: Las Palmas first team at 16 (Segunda División). Sold to Barcelona at 17 for ~€5m. Many big clubs (including Real Madrid) had watched him at 14-15 but didn't sign him because of his frame.
academy_bio.18-21: Barcelona first-team debut at 17. Started for Spain at the Euros at 18. Euro 2020 Young Player of the Tournament. Has battled hamstring issues from playing too many minutes too young.

attacking midfielder.career_brief: Career: La Masia at 17. Barcelona first-team debut at 17. Euro 2020 Young Player of the Tournament. Kopa Trophy 2021 (best U21 player in the world). 180+ Barcelona appearances by 22. Euro 2024 winner with Spain. FBref career pass completion ~91%.

attacking midfielder.name: De Bruyne-type chance creator
attacking midfielder.summary: Chance-creating machine — playing as a #10 his vision becomes lethal.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined KVV Drongen youth (small Belgian club) at age 6. Moved to Gent at 9-10 — known locally for hitting passes other kids his age couldn't even attempt.
academy_bio.11-12: Joined Genk academy at 11 — Genk being the top Belgian academy at the time alongside Anderlecht.
academy_bio.13-14: U13-U14 at Genk — was already striking the ball with the technique of a senior. Lived in academy housing during the week.
academy_bio.15-17: Genk youth → first-team debut at 17 (Belgian Pro League). Sold to Chelsea at 21 — never broke through, sent on loan to Werder Bremen.
academy_bio.18-21: Werder Bremen loan transformed him. Sold to Wolfsburg at 22, Bundesliga player of the season at 23. Manchester City at 24.

attacking midfielder.career_brief: Career: 400+ Manchester City appearances · 6× Premier League champion · 2× PFA Player of the Year (2019-20, 2021-22) · FBref top-5 all-time PL assist leader · UEFA Champions League winner 2022-23. Career assists per 90 in the PL: 0.38 (one of the highest ever recorded for an outfield player).

attacking midfielder.name: Bruno Fernandes-type chaos
attacking midfielder.summary: High-risk high-reward chaos creator — every action could be the killer ball.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined Boavista (Porto, Portugal) youth at age 8. Played up two age groups consistently because he was bigger physically.
academy_bio.11-12: U12 at Boavista — already showing the volume-shooting habit. Would attempt long-range shots multiple times a game even at U12.
academy_bio.13-14: U13-U14 at Boavista's academy — relentless work rate flagged by coaches. Wasn't flashy technically but always influenced games.
academy_bio.15-17: Moved to Italy at 17 (Novara, Serie B) on a youth contract — unusually direct route, bypassing the Portuguese senior academy.
academy_bio.18-21: Udinese at 18 (Serie A). Sampdoria at 22. Back to Portugal (Sporting CP) at 22 — became Portugal's player of the year before joining Manchester United at 25.

attacking midfielder.career_brief: Career: 400+ Manchester United appearances since 2020 · United captain since 2023 · Portugal captain. Most goal involvements in the PL across his first three seasons (after Salah, KdB). Has averaged 12+ PL assists per season at United (FBref).

attacking midfielder.name: Bellingham-type complete 8
attacking midfielder.summary: Generational midfielder — arrives in the box, defends, leads, scores.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined Birmingham City academy at 7 — local boy, his dad and brother both played for nearby teams.
academy_bio.11-12: U12 at Birmingham — already a head taller than peers and physically dominant. Captained his age group from U11 onwards.
academy_bio.13-14: U13-U14 at Birmingham — training regularly with the U18s. Birmingham retired his shirt number when he left — first English club to do so for an academy product.
academy_bio.15-17: Birmingham senior debut at 16 (Championship). Captained Birmingham at 17. Sold to Borussia Dortmund at 17 for £25m — record fee for an English 17-year-old.
academy_bio.18-21: Bundesliga player of the year-equivalent at 18. Real Madrid at 19 for £100m+. Champions League and La Liga winner at 20.

attacking midfielder.career_brief: Career: Birmingham → Dortmund → Real Madrid (2023, ~€103m). La Liga top scorer joint-runner-up in his debut Madrid season. England No. 10. La Liga 2023-24 champion + UCL 2023-24 champion in his first Madrid season. Kopa Trophy 2023. La Liga goals per 90 in season 1: ~0.65.

attacking midfielder.name: Foden-type inverted
attacking midfielder.summary: Plays multiple roles around the #10 with elite ball-carrying and finish.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined Manchester City academy at age 8. Local Stockport boy who would walk to Etihad Campus from a young age.
academy_bio.11-12: U12 at Man City — already drawing comparisons to David Silva in the academy. Coaches said his close control at 11 was 'unlike anyone we'd ever had'.
academy_bio.13-14: U13-U14 at City — winning every academy player of the year award. Trained with first team occasionally even at 14.
academy_bio.15-17: U18 captain at 16. Senior debut at 17 in the EFL Cup. England U17 World Cup-winning captain at 17 — best player at the tournament.
academy_bio.18-21: First Premier League start at 18. Champions League appearances at 19. By 21, established starter at Manchester City.

attacking midfielder.career_brief: Career: 250+ Manchester City appearances · 6× Premier League champion · FWA Footballer of the Year 2023-24 · PFA Young Player of the Year 2022-23 & 2023-24 (first ever back-to-back). Career goal+assist per 90 in the PL: ~0.70.

attacking midfielder.name: Jamal Musiala-type dribbler
attacking midfielder.summary: Carries the ball through any defence with feet too quick to follow.

academy_bio.8-10: Born in Germany, moved to England at 7. Joined Southampton youth at 8 — chosen over local Hampshire kids because of his close control.
academy_bio.11-12: Chelsea academy from 11. Lived in the Cobham academy housing — already standing out in the elite English youth setup.
academy_bio.13-14: U13-U14 at Chelsea — frequently played up two age groups. Eligible for England, Germany and Nigeria — England capped him first.
academy_bio.15-17: Surprise move to Bayern Munich at 16 — Chelsea couldn't guarantee a first-team pathway. Bayern senior debut at 17. Switched international allegiance to Germany at 18.
academy_bio.18-21: Bundesliga and Champions League regular by 19. Top scorer in the Bundesliga at 20. Considered the heir to Germany's #10 spot.

attacking midfielder.name: Lamine Yamal-type wonderkid
attacking midfielder.summary: Generational wonderkid — beats players and creates in equal measure.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined Barcelona's La Masia at age 7 — local Catalan kid (Mataró), spotted in a school competition.
academy_bio.11-12: U12 at La Masia — Xavi (then U10/U12 coach) reportedly told staff 'this one is different' when Yamal was 11.
academy_bio.13-14: U13-U14 La Masia — training with the older youth teams. La Liga staff already monitoring him for the senior squad pathway.
academy_bio.15-17: Barcelona B at 14. First-team debut at 15 years, 290 days — youngest in Barcelona history. Played at Euro 2024 at 16, becoming youngest goalscorer in tournament history.
academy_bio.18-21: Established starter for Barcelona at 16-17. Already in Ballon d'Or conversations at 17 — comparisons with the all-time greats are running ahead of his actual career.

attacking midfielder.career_brief: Career: Barcelona La Masia academy since age 7. La Liga debut at 15 (youngest in Barcelona history). Euro 2024 Young Player of the Tournament — youngest ever scorer at a Euros final. 16 years old when he debuted for Spain. Already 20+ Spain caps before turning 18.

attacking midfielder.name: Olise-type creator
attacking midfielder.summary: Left-foot magician — creates from wide #10 zones with elegant delivery.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined Chelsea academy at 8 — born in London to a French-Nigerian-Algerian family, multilingual upbringing.
academy_bio.11-12: U12 at Chelsea — already showing the left-foot delivery range that would define him later.
academy_bio.13-14: Released by Chelsea at U14 — deemed not athletic enough for the elite English pathway. Picked up by Reading academy.
academy_bio.15-17: Reading U18s. Senior debut at 16-17 in the Championship. Played in unfashionable lower-tier English football for several seasons.
academy_bio.18-21: Sold to Crystal Palace at 19 for ~£8m — Premier League breakthrough. Sold to Bayern Munich at 22 for ~€60m. A true 'rejected then redemption' story.

attacking midfielder.name: Kobbie Mainoo-type emerging 8
attacking midfielder.summary: Young academy prodigy with the composure of a senior midfielder.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined Manchester United academy at 9 — local Stockport boy (same area as Phil Foden).
academy_bio.11-12: U12 at United — already drawing comparisons within the academy for ball-retention under pressure.
academy_bio.13-14: U13-U14 at United — training regularly with the U18s.
academy_bio.15-17: United U18 captain at 17. Senior debut at 18 — Erik ten Hag fast-tracked him into the first team. FA Cup goal in the final at 18.
academy_bio.18-21: England senior debut at 18. Established Manchester United starter by 19 — quickest English academy product to break through in a decade.

attacking midfielder.name: Mahrez-type late breakthrough
attacking midfielder.summary: Late-blooming breakthrough — proves that not every elite career starts in elite academies.

academy_bio.8-10: Born in Paris suburbs (Sarcelles) — played street football through his pre-teen years. Never in a top French academy at this age.
academy_bio.11-12: Played for AAS Sarcelles (regional amateur club) — completely off the elite academy radar.
academy_bio.13-14: Still at AAS Sarcelles U14-U16 — slim build, no big-club interest. Family situation meant football was a hobby, not a project.
academy_bio.15-17: Late move to Quimper (Ligue 2 reserves) at ~18. Played in lower-tier French football — Le Havre B-side at 21. Still no Premier League radar.
academy_bio.18-21: Le Havre senior team. Leicester City scouted him at 23 in Ligue 2. Premier League title winner at 24-25. PFA Player of the Year same season. Manchester City for £60m at 27. Proves elite ceiling is achievable from semi-pro starts.

attacking midfielder.name: Florian Wirtz-type creator
attacking midfielder.summary: Creative engine — beats his man and finds the killer ball in the same motion.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined Köln youth at 7 — Pulheim local boy, near the Köln training ground.
academy_bio.11-12: U12 at Köln — known as one of the most technically advanced kids in the German youth pyramid.
academy_bio.13-14: U13-U14 at Köln academy — by U14 was widely regarded as the best youth prospect in Germany.
academy_bio.15-17: Surprise move to Bayer Leverkusen at 16 (Köln couldn't guarantee fast-track). Senior debut at 17. Bundesliga regular by 17-18.
academy_bio.18-21: ACL injury at 19 — recovered fully. Bundesliga title winner at 20 (Leverkusen's first ever). Real Madrid and Bayern interest at 21-22.

goalkeeper.name: Manuel Neuer-type sweeper
goalkeeper.summary: Plays the highest line in the league — sweeps behind the defence and starts attacks at his feet.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined Schalke 04 youth setup in Gelsenkirchen at age 5. Played outfield more than goal in small-sided games.
academy_bio.11-12: Committed to goalkeeping around U11 at Schalke. Already known for confident handling of the ball with his feet — unusual for that age.
academy_bio.13-14: U13–U14 Schalke 04 youth keeper. Tall and athletic for his age, organising the back line.
academy_bio.15-17: Germany U16/U17/U19 #1. Schalke senior bench from 17, professional contract at 17.
academy_bio.18-21: Schalke first-team debut at 20 (2006). Germany senior debut at 23. Bayern Munich at 25 for a then-record fee for a German keeper.

goalkeeper.career_brief: Career: 500+ Bayern Munich appearances · UEFA Champions League 2013 & 2020 · 11× Bundesliga titles · World Cup 2014 winner · IFFHS World's Best Goalkeeper 4×.

goalkeeper.name: Alisson-type modern keeper
goalkeeper.summary: Composure-first keeper who turns saves into counter-attacks within two passes.
goalkeeper.career_brief: Career: 300+ Liverpool appearances since 2018. UEFA Champions League winner 2018-19. PL champion 2019-20. Yashin Trophy 2019. PL Golden Glove 2018-19. Brazil's #1 keeper for the last 8+ years. FBref career save percentage in the PL: ~76%.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined Internacional youth in Porto Alegre, Brazil at age 7. Followed older brother Muriel (also a goalkeeper) into the club's academy.
academy_bio.11-12: Began focusing on goalkeeping around U12 at Internacional. Quiet, technically clean for his age.
academy_bio.13-14: Internacional U15 — already taller than most strikers he faced. Composed reading of crosses.
academy_bio.15-17: Internacional youth → senior bench at 19. Brazilian U17 squad.
academy_bio.18-21: Internacional senior debut at 20 (2013). Copa Libertadores semi-final run at 21. Roma signed him at 23.

goalkeeper.name: Courtois-type shot-stopper
goalkeeper.summary: Old-school commanding keeper whose size and timing make every save look routine.
goalkeeper.career_brief: Career: Real Madrid since 2018. UCL winner 2021-22 (named final's man of the match — 9 saves vs Liverpool). Yashin Trophy 2022. Belgium's all-time most-capped keeper. La Liga clean-sheet leader multiple seasons.

academy_bio.8-10: Local boys' football in Bree, Belgium. Father Thierry was a semi-pro volleyball player — height ran in the family.
academy_bio.11-12: Joined Genk academy at age 12 in 2004. Already noticeably tall for his age.
academy_bio.13-14: Genk youth — by 14 he was around 1.95m, dominating crosses and one-on-ones in U15/U17.
academy_bio.15-17: Genk senior debut at 17 in 2009 — youngest #1 in Belgian Pro League history that season.
academy_bio.18-21: Won Belgian Pro League at 18, signed by Chelsea at 19. Loaned to Atlético Madrid for 3 years and won La Liga at 21.

goalkeeper.name: Ter Stegen-type passer
goalkeeper.summary: Treats build-up like a midfielder — both-footed range opens up the press.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined Borussia Mönchengladbach youth at age 4 — a local boy in his hometown club.
academy_bio.11-12: Switched to permanent goalkeeping around U12 at Gladbach. Already comfortable receiving back-passes under pressure.
academy_bio.13-14: Gladbach U15 captain. Coaches praised his decision-making with the ball at his feet.
academy_bio.15-17: Bundesliga debut at 18. Stayed and grew at the club rather than chasing big moves.
academy_bio.18-21: Gladbach #1 from 18 to 22. Barcelona signed him at 22 to learn under Bravo, then took over as #1 at 24.

goalkeeper.career_brief: Career: 350+ Barcelona appearances · UEFA Champions League 2015 winner · 5× La Liga · 5× Copa del Rey · Best UCL goalkeeper 2014-15.

goalkeeper.name: Mike Maignan-type athlete
goalkeeper.summary: Athletic shot-stopper who turns recoveries into impossible saves with raw pace.

academy_bio.8-10: Born in French Guiana, moved to the Paris suburb of Villiers-sur-Marne as a young child. Local AS Villiers football from age 6-7.
academy_bio.11-12: Spotted by PSG scouts around age 11-12. Joined PSG academy.
academy_bio.13-14: PSG U15. Athletic, tall, vocal — all the classic GK markers early.
academy_bio.15-17: PSG youth → senior bench by 17 as Sirigu/Salvatore's understudy.
academy_bio.18-21: Senior PSG appearances limited. Lille signed him at 20 in 2015 for regular Ligue 1 minutes.

goalkeeper.career_brief: Career: Ligue 1 title with Lille 2020-21 · Serie A title with AC Milan 2021-22 · UEFA Nations League 2021 with France · Yashin Trophy nominee 2022.

goalkeeper.name: Donnarumma-type reflex
goalkeeper.summary: Tall, springy keeper whose reflexes win the moments others can't even reach.

academy_bio.8-10: Local boys' football in Castellammare di Stabia, southern Italy. Older brother Antonio also a goalkeeper.
academy_bio.11-12: Played for ASD Club Napoli juniors. Already very tall for his age.
academy_bio.13-14: Signed by AC Milan academy at 14 (relatively late — physical development was already pro-grade).
academy_bio.15-17: Milan Primavera at 15-16. Serie A debut at 16 years 8 months in October 2015 — youngest goalkeeper to start a Serie A match.
academy_bio.18-21: Milan #1 from 16 onward. Italy senior debut at 17. Euro 2020 winner at 22, PSG move that same summer.

goalkeeper.career_brief: Career: 250+ club appearances · UEFA Euro 2020 winner & tournament Player of the Tournament · UEFA Champions League 2024-25 winner with PSG · Serie A debut at 16y 8m (youngest GK ever).

goalkeeper.name: David Raya-type distributor
goalkeeper.summary: Conducts the back four with both feet and intelligent claiming on crosses.

academy_bio.8-10: Grew up in Pallejà near Barcelona. Played at La Damm and local Catalan youth clubs from age 8.
academy_bio.11-12: Trial at Cornellà and Sant Boi — local football, no headline academy.
academy_bio.13-14: Decision around 14-15 to move to England — joined Blackburn Rovers academy at 16.
academy_bio.15-17: Blackburn academy → first-team bench at 18. Loaned to Southport (non-league) at 19 to get senior minutes.
academy_bio.18-21: Blackburn #1 at 20-21 in the Championship. Brentford signed him at 23, promoted to PL.

goalkeeper.career_brief: Career: 100+ Arsenal appearances · Promotion to Premier League with Brentford 2021 · Premier League Golden Glove 2023-24 (shared) · Spain senior squad.

goalkeeper.name: Jan Oblak-type positional
goalkeeper.summary: Saves through angles, not athleticism — the cleanest positional keeper in Europe.

academy_bio.8-10: Local football in Škofja Loka, Slovenia. Sister Teja (basketball) and the whole family are athletes.
academy_bio.11-12: Joined Olimpija Ljubljana youth around U12.
academy_bio.13-14: Olimpija academy keeper — physically advanced and exceptionally calm.
academy_bio.15-17: Slovenian senior debut at 16 with Olimpija. Benfica signed him at 17 in 2010.
academy_bio.18-21: Four loan spells with Beira-Mar, Olhanense, União de Leiria and Rio Ave from 18-21 — earned his way up before Benfica recall at 21.

goalkeeper.career_brief: Career: 400+ Atlético Madrid appearances · 2× La Liga · 4× Zamora Trophy (fewest goals conceded in La Liga) · Slovenia captain.

goalkeeper.name: Ederson-type playmaker
goalkeeper.summary: Plays like an extra deep-lying playmaker — pinpoint long range from his own box.

academy_bio.8-10: Local São Paulo state youth football in Osasco from age 7.
academy_bio.11-12: Joined São Paulo FC academy at 8 — released at 14 for being 'too small' physically.
academy_bio.13-14: Took the unusual step of moving to Portugal at 15 — signed by lower-division Ribeirão.
academy_bio.15-17: Ribeirão → Benfica B at 17 after a Portuguese scout flagged him.
academy_bio.18-21: Rio Ave loan at 19 (regular Primeira Liga minutes), Benfica recall at 21 — became Benfica's #1 in the famous play-out-from-the-back system.

goalkeeper.career_brief: Career: 250+ Manchester City appearances · 6× Premier League · UEFA Champions League 2023 winner · Copa América 2019 · pioneer of the modern sweeper-distributor goalkeeper.

centre back.name: Van Dijk-type leader
centre back.summary: Defends with brain and presence first — the modern complete leader CB.
centre back.career_brief: Career: Celtic → Southampton → Liverpool (~€84m, world-record CB fee at the time). PFA Player of the Year 2018-19 (only defender since 2005 to win it). UCL winner 2018-19, PL champion 2019-20. Netherlands captain. FBref career duels won per 90: ~6.5 in the PL.

academy_bio.8-10: Local Breda youth football in the Netherlands. WDS '19 amateur club.
academy_bio.11-12: Willem II youth — released around U16/17 for being 'too slow and weak'.
academy_bio.13-14: Willem II academy — modest reputation.
academy_bio.15-17: Groningen senior team at 19 (washed dishes at a restaurant alongside football early on).
academy_bio.18-21: Groningen at 19-21. Celtic at 22 — late developer who only became elite from age 22+. Liverpool at 26 for a world-record CB fee.

centre back.name: Rüdiger-type enforcer
centre back.summary: Plays on the front foot — closes ground in two steps and wins every duel he enters.

academy_bio.8-10: Local Berlin football — Brandenburg youth clubs.
academy_bio.11-12: Signed by VfB Stuttgart academy at 12 after impressing in youth tournaments.
academy_bio.13-14: Stuttgart U17 — physically imposing already.
academy_bio.15-17: Stuttgart senior debut at 18 in 2012.
academy_bio.18-21: Stuttgart at 18-21, Roma at 22, Chelsea at 24, Real Madrid at 28.

centre back.name: Bastoni-type ball-player
centre back.summary: A Serie A modern CB who builds attacks like a deep-lying midfielder.

academy_bio.8-10: Local Casalmaggiore youth football near Cremona, Italy.
academy_bio.11-12: Atalanta academy from age 12 — already cultured on the ball.
academy_bio.13-14: Atalanta Primavera — Italian youth team regular at 14-15.
academy_bio.15-17: Atalanta senior debut at 17 in 2017. Inter Milan signed him at 18 for €32m.
academy_bio.18-21: Loan back to Atalanta then Parma, before becoming Inter's regular starter at 21 in 2020.

centre back.name: Saliba-type complete CB
centre back.summary: The blueprint for the modern CB — pace, positioning and elite ball-playing.
centre back.career_brief: Career: Saint-Étienne → Arsenal at 19. Three loan spells (Saint-Étienne, Nice, Marseille) before breaking in at 21. Arsenal Player of the Season 2022-23. French senior squad regular since 22. PL fewest goals conceded as a CB starter in 2023-24.

academy_bio.8-10: Local football in Bondy and Beauvais area, France. AS Bondy youth — same club as Mbappé.
academy_bio.11-12: Joined Saint-Étienne youth at 12.
academy_bio.13-14: Saint-Étienne academy U15.
academy_bio.15-17: Saint-Étienne senior debut at 17 in 2018 in Ligue 1.
academy_bio.18-21: Arsenal signed him at 18 for €30m, loaned back to Saint-Étienne, then Nice and Marseille from 18-21. Arsenal first-choice at 21 in 2022.

centre back.name: Kim Min-jae-type aggressor
centre back.summary: Asian CB who proves the modern game needs aerobic CBs — duels, sprints, repeats.

academy_bio.8-10: South Korean youth football in Tongyeong region.
academy_bio.11-12: Tongyeong Middle School football team — late starter in formal academies.
academy_bio.13-14: Suwon Technical High School football.
academy_bio.15-17: Yonsei University football at 17-18 — South Korea's main university football pathway.
academy_bio.18-21: Gyeongju KHNP semi-pro at 20, Jeonbuk Hyundai at 21 — South Korean Player of the Year. Beijing Guoan, then Fenerbahçe at 25, Napoli at 26 (Serie A title), Bayern at 27.

centre back.name: Araújo-type athletic CB
centre back.summary: Defends a high line confidently because his recovery pace covers most threats.

academy_bio.8-10: Local Rivera youth football, Uruguay-Brazil border region.
academy_bio.11-12: Modest local clubs — no big academy involvement yet.
academy_bio.13-14: Joined Rentistas (Montevideo, 2nd tier) youth at 14-15.
academy_bio.15-17: Rentistas senior debut at 18 in Uruguayan league.
academy_bio.18-21: Boston River loan at 19, Barcelona B at 19 in 2018. Barcelona first team at 20.

centre back.name: Stones-type inverted CB
centre back.summary: Inverts into midfield mid-possession — redefines what CB technicality means.

academy_bio.8-10: Local Penistone Church youth football in South Yorkshire.
academy_bio.11-12: Barnsley academy from age 11.
academy_bio.13-14: Barnsley youth — composed on the ball, technically clean for his age.
academy_bio.15-17: Barnsley senior debut at 17 in Championship.
academy_bio.18-21: Everton signed him at 18 for £3m. England U21 captain at 20, senior debut at 20. Manchester City at 22.

centre back.name: Marquinhos-type reader
centre back.summary: Defends with the brain — reads the game two moves ahead, leads the line vocally.

academy_bio.8-10: Local São Paulo state youth football.

academy_bio.13-14: Clairefontaine national centre at 11-13 — already producing highlight clips. Signed by AS Monaco at 14.
academy_bio.15-17: Monaco senior debut at 16 (December 2015) — youngest first-team player in Monaco history. Senior breakthrough at 17 under Leonardo Jardim.
academy_bio.18-21: Ligue 1 title with Monaco at 17. PSG initially as a loan at 18 then €180m permanent. World Cup winner at 19 in 2018.

striker.name: Harry Kane-type deep-lying
striker.summary: Plays as a #9 + #10 hybrid — drops deep, links play, finishes chances.
striker.career_brief: Career: Tottenham all-time top scorer (213 PL goals — 2nd all-time after Shearer). 3× PL Golden Boot. England's all-time top scorer. Bundesliga 2023-24: 36 goals in 32 league games. Career club goals per 90: ~0.70.

academy_bio.8-10: Joined Arsenal academy at 8 — released after one season for being 'a little chubby'. Then Watford and Tottenham.
academy_bio.11-12: Joined Tottenham academy at 11 — the club he supported as a boy. Often played up an age group.
academy_bio.13-14: Spurs U14 — known for his finishing in volume training drills, not for speed.
academy_bio.15-17: Spurs U18 captain at 17. League Cup debut at 17.
academy_bio.18-21: Loaned to Leyton Orient (League One), Millwall, Norwich and Leicester from 18-21 — toughened him up. Spurs senior breakthrough at 21.

striker.name: Lewandowski-type finisher
striker.summary: Pure technical executioner — finishes with whatever foot, from any angle.

academy_bio.8-10: Local Warsaw football — Partyzant Leszno, then MKS Varsovia. Father was a judo champion and amateur footballer.
academy_bio.11-12: MKS Varsovia U13 — small for his age, mostly known for his work ethic.
academy_bio.13-14: Delta Warsaw academy and Legia Warsaw youth trials — released for being 'physically weak'.
academy_bio.15-17: Znicz Pruszków youth (third tier) — finally settled. Senior debut at 17 in the Polish third division.
academy_bio.18-21: Top scorer in Polish third tier at 18, second tier at 19. Lech Poznań signed him at 19, Polish league title at 21, Borussia Dortmund at 22.

striker.name: Lautaro Martínez-type
striker.summary: Relentless presser — leads the front-line press AND finishes chances.

academy_bio.8-10: Local football in Bahía Blanca, Argentina. Liniers de Bahía Blanca youth from age 7.
academy_bio.11-12: Small in stature, played in older age groups. Already a finisher in age-group games.
academy_bio.13-14: Racing Club academy in Buenos Aires from age 14 — moved across the country alone.
academy_bio.15-17: Racing U17 → senior debut at 18 in 2016 Argentine Primera.
academy_bio.18-21: Racing senior breakthrough at 18-19. Inter Milan at 20 in summer 2018.

striker.name: Alexander Isak-type
striker.summary: Elegant complete striker — both-footed, intelligent movement, clinical finish.

academy_bio.8-10: Born in Solna, Sweden, of Eritrean descent. AIK youth from age 6.
academy_bio.11-12: AIK academy in Stockholm — naturally tall, already a striker.
academy_bio.13-14: AIK U15 — playing up and scoring against U17s.
academy_bio.15-17: AIK senior debut at 16 — youngest player to score in Allsvenskan history. Borussia Dortmund signed him at 17.
academy_bio.18-21: Limited minutes at Dortmund, loaned to Willem II (Eredivisie). Real Sociedad at 20 in La Liga — breakthrough season.

striker.name: Victor Osimhen-type
striker.summary: Athletic monster — beats defenders for pace, in the air, and on the ground.

academy_bio.8-10: Grew up in Olusosun, Lagos — extremely poor neighbourhood, sold water and newspapers to help family. Street football only at this age.
academy_bio.11-12: Picked up by Ultimate Strikers Academy in Lagos around 12.
academy_bio.13-14: Caught attention at U17 World Cup qualifiers — Nigeria U17 captain by 14-15.
academy_bio.15-17: Won 2015 U17 World Cup with Nigeria as top scorer (10 goals — joint tournament record). Wolfsburg signed him at 17.
academy_bio.18-21: Loaned out from Wolfsburg, breakthrough at Charleroi (Belgium) at 19. Lille at 20 — Ligue 1 hat-tricks earned €70m Napoli move at 21.

striker.name: Ollie Watkins-type complete
striker.summary: Modern English #9 — elite movement, consistent finishing, all-action work rate.

academy_bio.8-10: Local football in Newton Abbot, Devon — far from any big academy.
academy_bio.11-12: Exeter City development centre at 11.
academy_bio.13-14: Exeter City academy at 13-14 — modest scout traffic, no big-six interest.
academy_bio.15-17: Exeter senior debut at 18 in League Two. Loaned to Weston-super-Mare (non-league) for senior minutes at 18.
academy_bio.18-21: Brentford signed him at 21 from Exeter in 2017 — Championship breakout there over 3 seasons, Aston Villa at 24.

striker.name: Nicolas Jackson-type
striker.summary: Marauding striker — endless runs in behind stretch defensive lines thin.

academy_bio.8-10: Local Senegalese football in Banjul (Gambia) and Senegal — modest setup, no formal academy.
academy_bio.11-12: Casa Sports Ziguinchor youth in Senegal.
academy_bio.13-14: Casa Sports → spotted at youth tournaments by European scouts.
academy_bio.15-17: Moved to Spain at 18 to Casa Sports → Villarreal B trial.
academy_bio.18-21: Villarreal B in Segunda from 19. Villarreal first team at 21. Chelsea signed him at 22.

striker.name: Darwin Núñez-type chaos
striker.summary: Chaotic energy striker — high-xG misses but eventually everything goes in.

academy_bio.8-10: Grew up in Artigas on the Uruguay-Brazil border in modest circumstances. Local club football.
academy_bio.11-12: Joined Club Atlético Peñarol youth in Montevideo (4-hour bus from home).
academy_bio.13-14: Peñarol U15 — raw, fast, scoring in waves.
academy_bio.15-17: Peñarol senior debut at 17. Almería (Spanish 2nd) signed him at 19 in 2019.
academy_bio.18-21: Almería at 19-20, Benfica at 20 — Champions League knockout goals at 21 earned a £85m Liverpool move at 22.
